examples.ko: 저는 두 가지 일을 동시에 잘 못 해요.
examples.en: I'm not good at doing two things at once.
Two alarms went off at the same time.
The two of them spoke at the same time.
I'm studying English and Korean at the same time.
Press the two buttons at the same time.

explain: ‘같이’는 사람이 함께라는 뜻이고, ‘동시에’는 시간이 같다는 뜻이에요. 한 사람이 두 가지를 할 때도 ‘동시에’를 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: 같이 is about being together with someone; 동시에 is about the time being the same. One person can also do two things 동시에.

examples.en: I chatted with a friend over coffee.
I stayed up late chatting with my younger sibling.
At lunchtime I chat with my coworkers.

examples.ko: 어제 뭐 했어요? — 친구하고 수다만 떨었어요.
examples.en: What did you do yesterday? — I just chatted with a friend.

examples.ko: 친구들하고 수다 떠는 시간이 제일 즐거워요.
examples.en: The time I spend chatting with my friends is the most fun.

explain: ‘수다를 떨다’처럼 꼭 ‘떨다’와 같이 써요. ‘이야기하다’보다 가볍고 편한 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: to be completely absorbed in chatting
phrases.nuance_ko: 시간 가는 줄 모르고 수다를 떨어요
phrases.nuance_en: used when friends chat so happily that they lose track of time
phrases.en_equiv: to be completely absorbed in chatting

explain_en: It almost always goes with 떨다: 수다를 떨다. It feels lighter and more relaxed than 이야기하다.

examples.ko: 음악 소리가 크면 문제에 집중할 수 없어요.
examples.en: If the music is loud, I can't focus on the questions.
When you're driving, focus only on driving.
Before an exam I just want to focus on studying.
In the library everyone quietly focuses on studying.

examples.ko: 동생이 게임에 집중해서 제 말을 못 들었어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling was so focused on the game that they didn't hear me.

explain_en: Say 공부에 집중하다, not 공부를 집중하다. The particle is 에.

examples.en: I jot down the important points while listening to lectures.
That professor's lectures are really popular.

examples.ko: 오늘 강의는 몇 시에 시작해요? — 열 시에 시작해요.
examples.en: What time does today's lecture start? — It starts at ten.

examples.ko: 온라인 강의를 들으면 집에서 공부할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you take an online lecture, you can study at home.
After the lecture ended, the students asked questions.

explain: 대학교나 학원에서 한 사람이 길게 설명하는 수업은 ‘강의’라고 해요. 초·중·고등학교 수업은 보통 ‘수업’이라고 해요.

explain_en: A long talk by one person at a university or academy is a 강의. Classes at elementary, middle and high school are usually called 수업.

examples.ko: 길을 건너기 전에 주변을 잘 봐요.
examples.en: Before crossing the street, I look around carefully.
There are lots of good places to eat around my office.

examples.ko: 집 주변에 공원이 있어서 자주 산책해요.
examples.en: There's a park near my house, so I often go for walks.
The people around me help me a lot.

examples.ko: 주변이 너무 시끄러워서 전화 소리가 안 들려요.
examples.en: It's so noisy around here that I can't hear the phone.

explain: ‘주위’와 거의 같아요. ‘주변 사람들’은 가족, 친구, 동료처럼 가까운 사람들이에요.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: It is almost the same as 주위. 주변 사람들 means the people close to you: family, friends, coworkers.

examples.en: On Sunday evenings, ironing is the most annoying chore.
Ironing takes a long time.
When the ironing is done, I hang the shirt on a hanger.
Before ironing, I check the iron's temperature.
I watched an ironing video and learned the steps.

explain: 도구는 ‘다리미’, 일은 ‘다림질’이에요. 옷을 다릴 때는 ‘다리다’라고 하고 ‘다려요’로 말해요.
explain_en: The tool is 다리미 and the chore is 다림질. The verb is 다리다, and in polite speech it becomes 다려요.
